title: Language switcher section (語言 / Language, 繁中|EN) is missing; the iOS locale is frozen at app start
web_ref: apps/web/src/app/app/settings/page.tsx:212-218 (Globe + '語言 / Language' + LanguageSwitcher, placed after BlockedUsers and before Privacy & Data); apps/web/src/components/nav/language-switcher.tsx:8-36
ios_ref: apps/ios/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:95-97 (BlockedUsersSection is followed directly by ExportDataSection); apps/ios/src/lib/i18n.ts:41-42 (activeLocale is a const computed once from the device locale)
current_ios: No language row. The app language can only follow the device language, and there is no in-app way to change it.
target: A card row between Blocked users and Privacy & Data: Globe 20 brandDeep + the literal '語言 / Language' (15/500 ink, the same bilingual literal web hard-codes) on the left. On the right, a 2-option segmented toggle with no sliding indicator: a container with hairline border, radius.sm and 2pt padding, holding '繁中' and 'EN' buttons (12/500, radius 6, paddingHorizontal 12, paddingVertical 4). The selected option uses colors.ink background with white text; the other uses ink2 text.
fix_plan: 1) In apps/ios/src/lib/i18n.ts change `export const activeLocale` to `export let activeLocale`. Add `setAppLocale(l: Locale)`, which sets i18n.locale and activeLocale, persists to AsyncStorage key 'mango.locale.v1' and notifies subscribers. Add `loadPersistedLocale()`, awaited in app/_layout.tsx before the first render (behind the existing ready gate). Babel's CJS interop reads `_i18n.activeLocale` at the use site, so the live binding works. 2) Add a LocaleContext in app/_layout.tsx whose value is used as the `key` of the root navigator, so the whole tree remounts with the new strings. 3) After a switch, write users/{uid}.locale = new locale (auth-profile already writes `locale: activeLocale`) so server pushes follow it. 4) Add a LanguageSwitcher component in apps/ios/src/components/settings/language-switcher.tsx and render it in settings.tsx after BlockedUsersSection. Alternative if the remount approach is rejected: set ios.infoPlist.CFBundleLocalizations ['zh-Hant','en'] in app.json and make the toggle call Linking.openSettings() to use iOS per-app language (needs a native rebuild, no new dependency).

title: Cancelling Google bind shows a 'binding failed' error, because google-signin v13 returns {type:'cancelled'} instead of throwing
web_ref: apps/web/src/components/auth/guest-upgrade.tsx:68-83 (cancel maps to errors.cancelled and is not treated as a failure)
ios_ref: apps/ios/src/lib/auth.ts:96-103 (buildGoogleCredential ignores the GoogleSignin.signIn() result, then getTokens() throws because no user is signed in); guest-upgrade-section.tsx:38-43 (only 'auth/canceled' and 'ERR_REQUEST_CANCELED' are treated as cancel); the installed @react-native-google-signin/google-signin is 13.3.1, whose signIn resolves {type:'cancelled'}
current_ios: A guest who opens the Google sheet and backs out gets a '綁定失敗，請稍後再試' alert. The same pattern likely affects the sign-in screen if it shares buildGoogleCredential.
target: Cancelling is silent, and real errors still alert.
fix_plan: In buildGoogleCredential: `const res = await GoogleSignin.signIn(); if (isCancelledResponse(res)) { const e = new Error('cancelled'); (e as any).code = 'auth/canceled'; throw e; }`. Import isCancelledResponse from the package (available in v13). Optionally use res.data.idToken directly instead of getTokens(). Also treat statusCodes.SIGN_IN_CANCELLED as cancel in guest-upgrade-section.tsx.

title: Cancelling Google or Apple sign-in shows a '登入失敗' error alert with the raw native message; error codes are not mapped
web_ref: apps/web/src/components/auth/sign-in-buttons.tsx:195-218 (friendlyError: cancelled→Auth.errors.cancelled, network, generic), 342-344 (inline red error text)
ios_ref: apps/ios/src/lib/auth.ts:29-38 and 94-101 (GoogleSignin.signIn() result ignored, then getTokens()); apps/ios/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx:34-37
current_ios: @react-native-google-signin v13.3.1 returns {type:'cancelled'} on cancel instead of throwing. The code ignores that result and calls getTokens(), which throws because no user is signed in, so a cancel surfaces as Alert('登入失敗', <native message>). Apple cancel throws ERR_REQUEST_CANCELED, which reaches the same Alert. The Firebase codes auth/account-exists-with-different-credential and auth/network-request-failed are shown raw. The same buildGoogleCredential path makes a Google cancel in the guest upgrade show errors.generic.
target: A cancel is silent, or at most shows inline Auth.errors.cancelled. Other errors show inline, centred red text under the buttons (colors.danger, 14), mapped to: network-request-failed → Auth.errors.network; account-exists-with-different-credential or credential-already-in-use → Auth.errors.differentCredential; operation-not-allowed → Auth.errors.providerDisabled; anything else → Auth.errors.generic.
fix_plan: In auth.ts, add class SignInCancelledError extends Error { code = 'auth/canceled' }. In signInWithGoogle and buildGoogleCredential, use const res = await GoogleSignin.signIn(); if (res.type !== 'success') throw new SignInCancelledError(); then use res.data.idToken, falling back to getTokens(). In sign-in.tsx, replace Alert.alert with const [error, setError] = useState<string|null>(null) and a friendlyError(code) helper: codes 'auth/canceled' and 'ERR_REQUEST_CANCELED' return null; the others map as listed above. guest-upgrade-section.tsx:39 already treats 'auth/canceled' as silent, so it starts working with no further change.

title: Family invite deep link is lost when the user is signed out (no ?next= equivalent)
current_ios: When the user is signed out and opens mangopet://join/123456, segments[0]==='join'. The root effect calls router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in'). After sign-in it replaces to /onboarding or /(tabs)/walks, so the code is dropped and joinFamilyByCode never runs.
target: After sign-in, the user is sent back to /join/<code> and the auto-join runs, matching web.
fix_plan: In RootNavigator, add const pendingJoinRef = useRef<string|null>(null). In the !user branch, before the replace, check segments[0]==='join'. If so, read the code from useGlobalSearchParams() or from segments, and store it in pendingJoinRef; also store it in AsyncStorage 'mango.pendingJoin' so it survives the Google or Apple app switch. In the decision block at lines 39-47, if a pending code exists, clear it and call router.replace(`/join/${code}`) instead of walks or onboarding.
